title: Transarterial periarticular embolization for osteoarthritis-related pain in the knee, elbow, hip, shoulder, and ankle joints
summary:
A transarterial periarticular embolization is to be performed on the study participants. 
For this purpose, a catheter is introduced into the arterial system via a thin needle, and the blood supply to the affected joint is visualized using a contrast medium injection. 
This allows pathological vessels, which form the basis for pain generation, to be identified and subsequently occluded via the catheter. 
A mixture of two antibiotics (imipenem/cilastatin) is used for this, which occludes the pathological vessels while simultaneously preventing local inflammation. 
Approximately 4 arteries are occluded per procedure. 
The procedural time is approximately 60 minutes. 
Following successful embolization, the catheter is removed, and the puncture site is closed manually and a compression bandage is applied.

interventions.name:
The aim of this study is to substantiate the previously published positive case reports regarding this innovative pain therapy within the framework of a structured and systematic prospective trial.

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
- Written informed consent of the study participant
- Clinically (orthopedically) established indication for interventional pain therapy of the affected joint
Exclusion criteria:
- Patients under 18 years of age
- PregnancyUncontrollable hypersensitivity to iodinated contrast media and/or local anesthetics, analgesics, sedatives, imipenem, or cilastatin
- Permanent anticoagulation or bleeding disorders (aPTT > 50 s; Quick value < 50%; platelet count < 50,000/µL)
- Acute infections (signs of infection, fever > 38.0 °C)
